advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the `fields()` discovery call through `_call_logged`/`_with_connection_retry` so its errors are translated, retried, and logged like every other transport REST call.
evidence: transport.py:711-716: `lister = getattr(self._client, "fields", None)` ... `self._epic_link_field_id = next((f.get("id") for f in lister() if f.get("name") == "Epic Link"), None)` — `lister()` is called outside `_call_logged`

retry.py:211-214: `This is ALSO the transport's single translation choke point: every method of :class:`JiraDataCenterTransport` routes its library call through here, so converting the unretried HTTP error to :class:`BackendHTTPError` here ... is what stops a vendor exception escaping the adapter.`

dispatch_one.py:553: `except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:` (HTTP-400 hierarchy arm) — an untranslated JIRAError skips this and hits dispatch_one.py:594 `except Exception` -> `outbound-parent-failed`
All sibling reads route through the choke point, e.g. transport.py:698 `issue = _call_logged("set_parent", remote_id, lambda: self._client.issue(remote_id))`
advisory.finding: The new field-discovery REST call `self._client.fields()` (`lister()`) is invoked directly, bypassing `_call_logged`/`_with_connection_retry` — the documented single translation choke point that converts vendor `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` into `BackendHTTPError(urllib.error.HTTPError)`. Every other REST call in this transport routes through it. A `JIRAError` raised while enumerating fields (e.g. HTTP 403/500, or an HTTP-400) escapes untranslated: it is NOT a `urllib.error.HTTPError`, so `dispatch_one` misses its `except urllib.error.HTTPError` 400 arm and classifies it via the bare `except Exception` as the retryable `outbound-parent-failed` rather than any accurate kind, and the call also gets no connection retry and no WARNING log.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the enumeration, e.g. `raw_fields = _call_logged("set_parent", remote_id, lambda: lister())` and then compute the match from `raw_fields`, so a `JIRAError` becomes a `BackendHTTPError` and is retried/logged at the choke point.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the field-inventory iteration with `isinstance(f, dict)` (matching the live helper) so a non-dict entry cannot raise AttributeError out of set_parent.
evidence: transport.py:715-718: `self._epic_link_field_id = next((f.get("id") for f in lister() if f.get("name") == "Epic Link"), None)` — no `isinstance(f, dict)` guard
tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py:1182: `(str(f.get("id")) for f in body if isinstance(f, dict) and f.get("name") == name)` — the sibling helper DOES guard
transport.py:721-725 comment: an `AttributeError` here must instead be a `NotImplementedError` so dispatch_one classifies it as `outbound-parent-unrepresentable`, not `outbound-parent-failed`
transport.py:707-718: only `if self._epic_link_field_id is _MISSING:` triggers a lookup; a cached `None` is never re-probed

transport.py:239-241 comment: `A lookup that finds nothing is cached too ... so a fieldless instance is not re-probed` — intentional, but does not distinguish a transient/partial empty result from a genuinely fieldless instance
backend.py:279: transport is constructed per backend/pass, so the poisoned `None` persists across all set_parent calls in that pass
advisory.finding: The field-matching generator calls `f.get("id")`/`f.get("name")` without guarding that each element is a dict, unlike the live-test helper `_named_field_id`, which guards with `isinstance(f, dict)`. If a real `fields()` response contains a non-dict element, `f.get` raises `AttributeError`, which (per this change's own stated contract) reaches `dispatch_one` as the wrong, retryable `outbound-parent-failed` classification.
merged_from: A successful-but-incomplete `fields()` response (transiently omitting 'Epic Link', or a permission-scoped inventory) permanently caches `None` for the transport's lifetime (a whole pass), so every subsequent epic reparent in that pass is declined as unrepresentable even though the field exists. Only genuine 'not-yet-looked-up' (`_MISSING`) is re-probed; a `None` result is never revisited.
advisory.suggested_fix: `next((f.get("id") for f in lister() if isinstance(f, dict) and f.get("name") == "Epic Link"), None)`
